intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded coves for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Algarve sea caves, including the famous Benagil Cave with its natural skylight dome. A guided kayak tour takes you along the dramatic coastline, through hidden grottos and arches inaccessible by foot.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting at Quinta dos Vales
experiences.description: Visit one of the Algarve's premier wine estates set among rolling hills and vineyards. Enjoy a guided tasting of regional wines including Negra Mole and Arinto varieties, paired with local cheeses and charcuterie, while touring the sculpture-dotted estate grounds.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour & Barrier Island Beaches
experiences.description: Take a scenic boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park teeming with birdlife and unique ecosystems. Disembark on pristine barrier island beaches like Ilha Deserta or Ilha de Tavira, accessible only by boat, for a secluded beach day.

experiences.name: Lagos Old Town Food & Wine Evening Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through the charming cobblestone streets of Lagos historic center on a guided evening food and wine tour. Sample regional Algarve wines from local producers alongside traditional petiscos such as cataplana seafood stew, grilled sardines, and pastel de nata at curated local spots.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Faro Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly bus (Eva/Rede Expressos) or shared shuttle to Lagoa/Carvoeiro area (~1.5 hrs, ~€8-12). Check in to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay. Drop luggage and take a short 10-minute walk down to Praia da Marinha beach for a first look at the stunning golden limestone cliffs and turquoise waters. No swimming gear needed — just soak in the view and decompress from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the village of Carvoeiro (5-min drive or 30-min walk) for a relaxed first evening. Explore the charming main square and small boardwalk overlooking Praia de Carvoeiro.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack at the airport — pastel de nata (€1.20) and coffee (€0.80) at a café kiosk.
meals.lunch: Pick up a prego roll (steak sandwich, ~€3.50) or bifana from a local tasca near the bus stop in Lagoa town during transit.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — local grilled fish (peixe grelhado) with salad and house wine, ~€12-15 per person. Ask for the 'prato do dia' (dish of the day) for best value.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 7-day or top-up Rede Expressos bus card if you plan to use buses frequently. September weather in Algarve is excellent — warm (~26°C), sunny, and sea still warm enough to swim. Exchange some cash at the airport (ATM is cheapest method). Stock up on water and snacks at a local mini-mercado to save money during the trip.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head to Praia da Marinha — one of Portugal's most beautiful beaches and just steps from your accommodation. Arrive early (before 10:00) to claim a good spot among the limestone rock formations. Swim, snorkel (bring your own or rent locally for ~€5), and explore the sea caves and arches accessible by foot at low tide. Check tide times the night before.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail) — a free, stunning 5.7 km coastal cliff walk starting near Praia da Marinha heading west toward Praia de Vale Covo, Praia de Benagil, and beyond. The views are world-class. Bring water and sun cream. Takes about 2-2.5 hours at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the accommodation to freshen up. Head to Lagoa town centre (10-min drive/bus) for a relaxed evening walk through the quiet, authentic town square — far fewer tourists than Carvoeiro or Albufeira.

meals.breakfast: At your accommodation or a local café — galão (milky coffee, €1.20) and toast with butter and jam (€1.50) at Café Central in Lagoa.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local mini-mercado: crusty bread, local cheese (queijo), cured meats, olives, and fruit — total ~€5 per person. Eat on the cliffs with a view.
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Lagoa — a no-frills local restaurant loved by residents. Grilled chicken (frango grelhado) with fries and salad, ~€8-10. House wine carafe ~€4.

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys trail is free but can be hot in September — start by 09:30 and carry at least 1.5L of water. Wear sturdy shoes as paths are rocky. The trail is one-way so arrange a return (taxi ~€8, or walk back the same route). Low tide access to sea caves at Praia da Marinha is magical — check tide tables on tideschart.com.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or taxi to Benagil (~15 min from Praia da Marinha). Join a budget kayak or SUP tour to the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil) — the most iconic cave in Portugal. Book in advance online with operators like Seafaris or Benagil Kayak Tours (~€15-20 per person for kayak rental/guided paddle). Alternatively, swim in from Praia de Benagil if you're a confident swimmer (check conditions first). Morning sessions are calmer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Praia de Benagil beach for a swim and relaxation. Then walk or take a taxi to Praia de Carvalho (a hidden gem with a tunnel entrance) — about 2 km west along the cliff path.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Carvoeiro village for the evening. Walk along the clifftop boardwalk (Passadiço de Carvoeiro) for sunset views. Browse the small shops and enjoy the lively but relaxed atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: At your accommodation or grab a pastry and espresso at a café near Benagil beach — bifana (pork roll) or croissant, ~€2-3.
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh grilled sardine sandwich or tosta mista (ham and cheese toastie) at one of the beach snack bars at Benagil (~€4-6).
meals.dinner: O Castelo Restaurant or Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — try cataplana (traditional Algarve seafood stew) shared between two people (~€18-22 for the pot, excellent value). House wine ~€5.

day_by_day.notes: Book Benagil kayak tours at least 1-2 days ahead in September — still busy season. Avoid expensive boat tours (€25-35) and opt for kayak/SUP for the budget-friendly and more adventurous option. The Benagil cave can only be entered from the water — you cannot walk in. Carvoeiro boardwalk is free and perfect for sunset photography.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve. Take the regional train from Lagoa station (€2.30 each way, 15 min) or bus. Visit the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry, free for under 12). Walk the ancient walls and enjoy panoramic views over the orange groves and the Arade River. The castle is one of the best-preserved Moorish fortifications in Portugal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves town on foot — visit the Gothic Cathedral (Sé Catedral de Silves, free entry), the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (€2.10), and stroll along the riverside promenade. Browse the local market area for fresh almonds, figs, and carob (September is harvest season). Walk across the ancient Roman bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa/Praia da Marinha by train or bus. Relax at the accommodation or take a sunset walk along the Marinha cliffs.

meals.breakfast: At the accommodation or Café Inglês in Silves (a charming café inside the castle walls) — coffee and pastry ~€2.50.
meals.lunch: Café Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a beloved local spot. Try the arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) or grilled dourada (sea bream) with potatoes and salad, ~€10-13. Very popular with locals.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the accommodation using fresh produce bought at Silves market (bread, local cheese, figs, olives, charcuterie) — budget dinner ~€5-7 per person. Pair with a bottle of local Algarve wine from the mini-mercado (~€4-6).

day_by_day.notes: Silves is an unmissable cultural stop and very budget-friendly. September coincides with the end of the Silves Medieval Festival (usually August) so check if any late events are scheduled. The train from Lagoa station is the cheapest and most scenic option. Buy train tickets at the station (no advance booking needed for regional trains). Bring cash as some small restaurants in Silves are cash-only.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Visit Adega do Cantor (Winery of the Singer — named after Sir Cliff Richard who owns it) near Guia/Albufeira (~20 min drive). Book a morning tour and tasting in advance (~€10-15 per person). The estate produces award-winning Vida Nova and Onda Nova wines. Alternatively, visit Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar (~15 min from Lagoa) — a stunning wine estate with sculptures, vineyard tours, and tastings from €12 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine theme with a visit to Quinta da Franceza or explore the Lagoa wine cooperative — Lagoa is actually the heart of Algarve wine production. The Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa offers tastings of local reds, whites, and the regional specialty medronho (arbutus berry spirit) at very affordable prices (~€5-8 for a tasting flight). Walk the surrounding vineyard trails.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Lagoa town for the Saturday evening passeio (evening stroll). The town comes alive with locals on weekends. Enjoy the relaxed atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: At the accommodation — bread, local honey, yogurt, and coffee. Many Algarve guesthouses provide basic breakfast. Budget ~€0 if included or €3-4 at a café.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery if offered, or pack a picnic with local wine, cheese, and bread to enjoy in the vineyard — ~€8-10 total.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Lagoa in the town centre — a traditional tasca with excellent value menú do dia (set menu: soup, main, dessert, and drink) for ~€10-12. Try the local lamb (borrego) or pork with clams (carne de porco à Alentejana).

day_by_day.notes: Book winery tours ahead, especially on Saturdays. Quinta dos Vales is particularly scenic and photogenic with its outdoor sculptures. Designate a non-drinking driver or arrange a taxi/Uber if visiting multiple wineries (Uber is available in the Algarve and reasonably priced). September is harvest season (vindima) — you may get to see or even participate in grape picking at some estates. This is a unique experience not to miss.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia de Albandeira and Praia de Centianes — two beautiful, quieter beaches accessible by car or a scenic cliff walk from Praia da Marinha (heading east). Albandeira has a natural arch and is less crowded. Spend the morning swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Armação de Pêra — a larger beach town 15 minutes west. Walk along the long sandy beach (one of the longest in the Algarve). Visit the small 17th-century fortress chapel (free). Browse the Sunday market if still running. The town has a more authentic, less touristy feel than Albufeira.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Praia da Marinha — walk to the cliff viewpoint just above the beach for one of the most spectacular sunsets in the Algarve. Bring a bottle of local wine from the mini-mercado and enjoy the golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Sunday morning treat — visit the weekly Lagoa market (Mercado de Lagoa) for fresh fruit, pastries, and local products. Budget ~€3-5 for a delicious spread.
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Armação de Pêra beach — fresh grilled fish, chips, and a cold Super Bock beer, ~€10-12.
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Forja in Armação de Pêra or cook at the accommodation. If eating out, try percebes (barnacles) or amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams in garlic and coriander) as a starter, ~€15-18 total for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a great day to visit local markets and enjoy a slower pace. Praia de Albandeira is accessible via a steep path — wear appropriate footwear. Armação de Pêra has a large supermarket (Continente or Pingo Doce) — good opportunity to stock up on supplies for the week at lower prices than mini-mercados. The cliff sunset at Praia da Marinha is genuinely one of the best in Portugal — don't miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — one of the most beautiful towns in the Algarve (~30 min by bus from Lagoa, €3.50 each way on Eva bus). Start with a walk through the historic old town: visit Igreja de Santo António (€4, includes town museum), the slave market museum (Mercado de Escravos, €3 — the only one of its kind in Europe), and the old city walls. Stroll through the cobbled streets and Praça Gil Eanes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi/bus to Ponta da Piedade — the most dramatic rock formation in the Algarve. Walk the clifftop path (free) for incredible views. Optionally rent a kayak or take a short boat trip (€10-15) to explore the sea caves and grottos up close. Visit Praia Dona Ana and Praia do Camilo (linked by a wooden staircase) for a swim.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Lagos town in the evening — it has a vibrant but relaxed vibe. Walk along the marina and enjoy the sunset over the Meia Praia estuary.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mota in Lagos old town — a classic local bakery. Coffee and pastel de nata or bola de Berlim (custard-filled doughnut), ~€2.50.
meals.lunch: Tasca do Celso in Lagos — a beloved hole-in-the-wall local eatery. Prato do dia (daily special) with soup, main, and drink for ~€8-9. Arrive before 12:30 as it fills up fast.
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant near Praia do Camilo (moderate budget splurge) — fresh grilled fish with views, ~€15-18. Or head back to Lagos centre for a more affordable option at Restaurante Adega da Marina (~€12-14 for a full meal).

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is a must-visit and very walkable. Buy bus tickets on the Eva Transportes app or at the station for the best price. Ponta da Piedade is free to visit but parking can be tight — walking from town (2.5 km) is a pleasant option. September means slightly shorter queues than August but it's still popular. Bring cash for smaller restaurants. Lagos has a lively nightlife scene if you want to extend your evening.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed beach morning at Praia da Marinha. This is your home beach — enjoy it without rushing. Try snorkelling around the rock formations (bring or rent gear). The water visibility in September is excellent. Practice identifying local marine life: octopus, sea urchins, and various fish are common.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Algar Seco rock formations near Carvoeiro — a stunning natural landscape of eroded limestone rocks, tunnels, and pools accessible via a free clifftop boardwalk. Very photogenic and unlike anywhere else in the Algarve. Then relax at Praia do Carvoeiro for the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class or visit a local wine bar in Carvoeiro. Alternatively, visit a local adega (wine cellar) in Lagoa for an informal tasting. Look for 'Adega Cooperativa do Algarve' events or simply buy a selection of local wines from the cooperative shop to taste at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: At the accommodation — yogurt, local honey, fresh figs (in season in September), and coffee.
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia do Carvoeiro — fresh fish soup (sopa de peixe, ~€4) and a bifana (~€3.50). Simple and delicious.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nortada in Carvoeiro — known for good value seafood. Grilled lulas (squid) or espetada (meat skewer) with salad and chips, ~€11-14. House wine carafe €4-5.

day_by_day.notes: Algar Seco is free and takes about 45 minutes to explore properly. Go at low tide for the best experience — you can walk through the tunnels and reach small natural pools. The boardwalk is accessible and well-maintained. This is a great photography spot — bring your camera. September figs are spectacular in the Algarve — look for roadside stalls selling them cheaply (€1-2 per bag).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of Europe and one of the most dramatic landscapes in Portugal (~1 hour by bus from Lagos, or arrange a day tour from Lagoa). Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — a vast clifftop fortress with an enormous wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos) and stunning Atlantic views. Watch migrating birds (September is peak migration season).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi (3 km) to Cabo de São Vicente — the most southwestern point of continental Europe. The lighthouse (free to visit the exterior) sits atop 75-metre cliffs with breathtaking views. Watch the waves crash against the rocks. Visit the small market stalls selling local crafts and smoked sausages. Then visit Praia do Martinhal or Praia de Sagres for a late afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa/Praia da Marinha. Enjoy a quiet evening at the accommodation or in Carvoeiro.

meals.breakfast: Early start — grab a coffee and pastry at the bus station café in Lagos or Lagoa before departure, ~€2.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Nort in Sagres village — a local favourite. Try atum (tuna) steak with vegetables (tuna is a Sagres speciality), ~€10-12. Or grab a sandwich from a local café to eat at the cape.
meals.dinner: Back at the accommodation — prepare a simple pasta with local ingredients bought from the market: canned tuna, olives, tomatoes, garlic — budget meal ~€4-5 per person. Pair with a bottle of Algarve white wine (~€5).

day_by_day.notes: Sagres requires an early start if going by public bus (check Eva Transportes timetable — limited service). Consider joining a budget day tour from Albufeira or Lagos (~€25-30 per person) that covers both Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente if bus connections are inconvenient. September is one of the best months for birdwatching at Sagres — raptors, storks, and passerines migrate through in large numbers. Bring a light jacket as the cape is windier than the rest of the Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Portimão — the largest city in the western Algarve (~20 min by bus from Lagoa, €2.50). Start at the Museu de Portimão (€3, free on Sunday afternoons) — an excellent museum built inside a former sardine canning factory, telling the story of the Algarve's fishing and canning industry. Very interesting and well-presented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the bridge to Ferragudo — a charming, largely untouristy fishing village with colourful boats, a 16th-century castle (Castelo de São João do Arade, exterior free), narrow cobbled streets, and excellent local restaurants. Swim at Praia de Ferragudo — a beautiful sandy beach with views back to Portimão.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Portimão for the evening. Walk along the riverside promenade and enjoy the local atmosphere. The Portimão marina area has free live music and events in September.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Garrett in Portimão — a classic old-school Portuguese café. Galão and croissant de amêndoa (almond croissant), ~€2.80.
meals.lunch: Ferragudo is famous for its seafood restaurants. Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — grilled fish of the day with salad and potatoes, ~€12-15. Sit on the terrace overlooking the river.
meals.dinner: Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines (sardinhas grelhadas). Try the riverside restaurants near the old fish market — a full sardine dinner with bread, salad, and wine costs ~€10-12. This is an authentic Algarve experience.

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is one of the most underrated villages in the Algarve — far less touristy than Carvoeiro or Albufeira. It's only a 10-minute walk across the bridge from Portimão. The Museu de Portimão is genuinely excellent and very good value. Portimão also has a large Continente supermarket — great for restocking budget food supplies. Check for the Portimão Sardine Festival schedule (usually August, but some events extend into September).

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — visit the Lagoa wine region more deeply. Take a self-guided cycling or walking tour of the vineyards around Lagoa and Estômbar. Rent a bike from a local shop in Carvoeiro (~€10-15/day) and follow the wine route (Rota dos Vinhos do Algarve). Stop at Quinta da Franceza or Quinta do Barranco Longo for a tasting (~€8-12).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Estômbar area and the beautiful Arade River. Take a short walk along the riverbank. Then relax at Praia da Marinha for a final long afternoon swim — savour the beach you've been staying near all week.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly for a nicer dinner to celebrate the penultimate full day. Head to Carvoeiro or Lagoa for a special meal.

meals.breakfast: At the accommodation — make a full Portuguese breakfast with ingredients from the market: bread, presunto (cured ham), local cheese, tomatoes, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic in the vineyards — buy local wine, cheese, bread, and fruit from the Lagoa cooperative shop or market, ~€8-10 total. Eat among the vines.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon in Carvoeiro (slight splurge — Michelin-starred but lunch/early dinner menus can be more affordable) OR opt for Restaurante A Muralha in Silves for a special evening of traditional Algarve cuisine with local wines, ~€20-25 per person for a full experience.

day_by_day.notes: The Rota dos Vinhos do Algarve is a mapped wine route — pick up a brochure from the Lagoa tourist office (free). Cycling between wineries is a wonderful way to see the countryside. September harvest season means some wineries offer special harvest experiences — call ahead to ask. If you prefer not to cycle, a taxi between 2-3 wineries is still budget-friendly (~€15-20 for the day shared between travellers).

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favourite beach of the trip. Praia da Marinha is the obvious choice for a last swim among the spectacular cliffs. Arrive early to have the beach more to yourself. Go snorkelling, explore the rock pools, and take final photos of the stunning scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Saturday market in Lagoa or Portimão for last-minute souvenir shopping. Look for: local honey (mel do Algarve), medronho spirit, local wine, almond products (Dom Rodrigo sweets), dried figs, and handmade ceramics. These are all affordable and authentic gifts. Browse the stalls and soak up the local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Carvoeiro or Lagoa. Celebrate 13 days in the Algarve with a proper Portuguese feast.

meals.breakfast: Final morning treat — visit a local pastelaria for a full Portuguese breakfast spread: orange juice, galão, pastel de nata, tosta mista, and fresh fruit, ~€5-6.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the beach snack bar — don't overeat as a big dinner is planned.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Barão in Lagoa — a beloved local institution. Order the mixed seafood platter (mariscada) to share between two (~€35-40 total for two, excellent value for the quantity and quality). Pair with a bottle of local Lagoa white wine. This is the perfect farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight for an easier morning tomorrow. Algarve honey and medronho make excellent and affordable souvenirs — buy from the market rather than tourist shops for much better prices. Check bus/transfer times to Faro Airport for the next morning. Book a taxi or shuttle in advance if your flight is early. Consider buying a bottle of Vida Nova wine or Lagoa cooperative wine to take home as a reminder of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Depending on flight time, take one last walk to the Praia da Marinha viewpoint at sunrise for a final look at the golden cliffs. Pack remaining items and check out of the accommodation. Take a slow coffee at a local café and reflect on an incredible 13-day trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Faro Airport. Allow at least 2-2.5 hours before flight departure for check-in and security. The Eva bus from Lagoa/Portimão to Faro takes about 1.5 hours and costs ~€5-7. Alternatively, a shared shuttle or taxi costs ~€25-35 from Lagoa area.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Board flight home with wonderful memories of Algarve beaches, wine, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and espresso at a café near the accommodation — a perfect last taste of Portugal, ~€2.
meals.lunch: Airport café or pack leftover market snacks (bread, cheese, fruit) for the journey.
meals.dinner: On the flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is usually 11:00 — confirm with your accommodation. If your flight is in the late afternoon or evening, you may be able to store luggage at the accommodation and enjoy a final few hours at the beach or in town. Faro Airport has a small but decent duty-free section where you can pick up last-minute Portuguese wine or port. Leave a review for your accommodation on Booking.com or Google — it helps small boutique stays enormously. Total estimated trip budget (excluding flights and accommodation): approximately €400-550 per person for 13 days, covering food, local transport, activities, and wine tastings.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at Faro Airport at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, rent a car (highly recommended for Algarve exploration), and drive approximately 45 minutes west to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique stay, freshen up, and take a gentle first walk down to Praia da Marinha — one of the most stunning cove beaches in the Algarve. Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and sea arches at a relaxed pace. Swim if the tide allows.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the village of Carvoeiro (10 min drive) for a sunset walk along the cliff boardwalk (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos trailhead). Enjoy the golden-hour light over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at Faro Airport café upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at a café near Faro Airport or a roadside pastelaria en route — try a bifana (pork sandwich) and a pastel de nata (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — mid-range, excellent fresh grilled fish and seafood, great sea views (€20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a car at Faro Airport — essential for navigating the Algarve. September is ideal: warm (26–28°C), fewer crowds than August, sea still warm. Stock up on water and snacks at a local Pingo Doce supermarket near Lagoa town.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, hike the famous Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys) coastal trail starting from Praia de Vale Centianes near Carvoeiro. This 6 km one-way cliff-top walk passes extraordinary rock formations, hidden coves, and sea caves. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water.
day_by_day.afternoon: End the hike at Praia da Marinha (or reverse it). Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing at Praia da Marinha itself — the beach is sheltered by cliffs and has crystal-clear turquoise water. Rent a kayak or take a short boat trip into the sea caves and grottos (local operators on the beach, ~€15–20 pp).
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Lagoa town (15 min) to explore the local wine scene. Visit the Lagoa Wine Cooperative (Adega Cooperativa do Algarve) — one of the oldest and most respected in the region — for an early-evening tasting of Algarve regional wines including Negra Mole and Arinto varieties.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay or a local café — toast, eggs, fresh fruit, galão coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or grab lunch at the beach snack bar at Praia da Marinha — grilled sardines, salad, and a cold Super Bock beer (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro area) — a beloved local spot with excellent cataplana (traditional Algarve seafood stew) and regional wines (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Sete Vales Suspensos trail is best done in the morning before the midday heat. Wear sunscreen. The Lagoa Cooperative offers tastings for around €5–10 — call ahead or check opening hours as they may vary by season.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Albufeira (30 min) and visit the Albufeira Old Town. Explore the charming whitewashed streets, the fishing quarter, and the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia. Walk down to Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) in the town center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Falésia (15 min east of Albufeira) — a spectacular 6 km stretch of beach backed by vivid red and ochre striped cliffs. This is one of the Algarve's most photogenic beaches. Swim, sunbathe, and walk along the shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Albufeira for the evening. Walk the lively Rua Candido dos Reis (the strip) and enjoy the buzzing atmosphere. Find a quieter spot in the old town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay or stop at a local padaria (bakery) in Carvoeiro for fresh bread, cheese, and coffee
meals.lunch: A Ruína restaurant in Albufeira Old Town — iconic cliffside location, fresh seafood, great value lunch menu (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Albufeira old town — rustic, authentic Portuguese petiscos (tapas-style dishes), local wines, very popular with locals (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Parking in Albufeira can be tricky — use the paid parking lots near the tunnel to the beach. Praia da Falésia is best accessed from the Olhos de Água end for a quieter experience.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west to Silves (20 min from Lagoa) — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Explore the ramparts and enjoy panoramic views over the orange and cork tree countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves further: visit the Gothic Sé Catedral de Silves and the Museu Arqueológico. Then drive 10 minutes to the Quinta do Francês winery for an afternoon wine tasting — a small boutique winery producing excellent Algarve wines in a beautiful rural setting. Book ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro for a relaxed evening. Walk the clifftop promenade at sunset and find a terrace bar for a glass of wine or a gin and tonic while watching the sun dip into the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay — full Portuguese breakfast
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — set in a beautiful restored building near the castle, great salads, local dishes, and wine (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: O Chefe in Carvoeiro — family-run, excellent grilled meats and fish, friendly atmosphere, very popular with locals (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a must-visit and often overlooked by tourists who stay on the coast. The Quinta do Francês winery visit typically costs €10–15 for a tasting — call ahead to confirm availability. September is harvest season, making wine visits especially interesting.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west to Portimão and take a boat trip from Portimão Marina into the Algar Seco rock formations and sea caves near Carrapateira. Alternatively, take a 2-hour catamaran cruise along the coastline from Portimão, passing sea caves, grottos, and the famous Ponta da Piedade cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha (Portimão) — one of the Algarve's most famous beaches — for an afternoon swim. The wide golden beach is backed by dramatic cliff formations. Walk along the clifftop promenade for great views.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for dinner. The Portimão waterfront (Ribeira) is famous for its sardine grilling tradition — September is the tail end of sardine season, a perfect time to enjoy them.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay or a café in Carvoeiro
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the boat trip, or grab a sandwich at the Portimão Marina before boarding
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré on the Portimão waterfront — excellent grilled sardines, fresh fish, and local wines in an authentic riverside setting (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Boat trips from Portimão Marina are plentiful — compare operators on the dock. Prices range from €20–35 per person for a 2-hour trip. Book the morning before or the day before on weekends. Portimão is a 20-minute drive from Praia da Marinha.

day_by_day.morning: Take a leisurely morning at Praia da Marinha — a perfect beach day. Explore the rock pools at low tide, snorkel in the clear water, and enjoy the dramatic scenery. This is a great day to relax after several active days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Ferragudo (20 min east of Portimão) — a charming, unspoiled fishing village with whitewashed houses, a 16th-century castle, and a lovely beach (Praia Grande de Ferragudo). Wander the cobbled streets and enjoy the authentic village atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a quiet Sunday evening back near the boutique stay. Visit a local wine shop in Lagoa town and pick up a bottle of regional wine to enjoy on your terrace or room balcony.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay — take it slow on a Sunday
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia da Marinha or a picnic on the beach with local cheeses, cured meats, and bread from a Lagoa supermarket
meals.dinner: Sueste restaurant in Ferragudo — riverside terrace, outstanding fresh fish and seafood, beautiful views of the Portimão estuary (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is one of the Algarve's hidden gems — far less touristy than its neighbors. Sunday afternoons can be lively with local families. The castle (Castelo de São João de Arade) can be admired from outside — check if interior visits are available.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west to Lagos (35 min) — one of the most beautiful historic towns in the Algarve. Explore the well-preserved old town: the Igreja de Santo António (stunning gilded baroque interior), the Museu Municipal, and the ancient city walls and fortifications.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Lagos town to Ponta da Piedade (2 km) — the most spectacular coastal landmark in the Algarve. The golden limestone sea stacks, arches, and grottos are extraordinary. Take a short kayak or boat trip from the Ponta da Piedade steps into the caves (~€10–15 pp). Then visit Praia Dona Ana — a stunning sheltered cove just north of Ponta da Piedade.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for the evening. The town has a vibrant but not overwhelming nightlife and excellent restaurants.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay before departing
meals.lunch: : Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — a beloved local lunch spot with daily specials, great value, very popular with locals (€12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Vitor's Restaurant in Lagos — long-standing institution, excellent cataplana and regional cuisine, great wine list (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is a full day's destination — arrive early to avoid the midday rush at Ponta da Piedade. Parking is available near the marina. The old slave market (Mercado de Escravos) near the waterfront is a sobering and important historical site worth visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Drive further west to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente (1 hour from Lagoa) — the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress used by Henry the Navigator to plan the Age of Discovery. Walk the windswept cliffs of Cabo de São Vicente — the most southwesterly point of Europe — for stunning Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres town and its wild, unspoiled beaches: Praia do Martinhal and Praia da Mareta are both excellent. The Costa Vicentina (west coast) beaches near Sagres are wilder and less developed — try Praia do Beliche for a dramatic clifftop setting.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back east toward Lagoa. Stop in Lagos for a glass of wine at a wine bar before heading back to the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay before the early drive
meals.lunch: A Sagres — simple, excellent fresh fish restaurant in Sagres village, very popular, great value (€15–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega Vila Lisa in Mexilhoeira Grande (on the way back, near Portimão) — rustic wine estate restaurant, exceptional regional food and local wines in a beautiful setting (€22–30 per person) — reservations recommended

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is the windiest point in Portugal — bring a light jacket even in September. The drive along the Costa Vicentina is spectacular. Allow 2 hours for the round trip from Lagoa. This is a long but rewarding day — start early.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wine day. Drive to the Monchique mountains (45 min north of Portimão) for a morning excursion. Visit the charming spa town of Caldas de Monchique — a shaded valley with a natural mineral spring, historic buildings, and a peaceful atmosphere very different from the coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up to the summit of Fóia (902m) — the highest point in the Algarve — for panoramic views stretching from the coast to the Spanish border on a clear day. On the way back down, stop at a local quinta (farm estate) near Monchique for a tasting of medronho — the local firewater made from arbutus berries — and local honey and jams.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast and drive to Lagoa for a proper wine tasting dinner. The Algarve's wine region is centered around Lagoa — visit a wine bar or restaurant specializing in regional wines.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Restaurante 1692 in Caldas de Monchique — set in a historic building, excellent regional mountain food including smoked sausages, black pork, and local cheeses (€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Adega do Cantor (near Guia, 20 min east) — the famous winery restaurant associated with Cliff Richard's Quinta do Miradouro, excellent Algarve wines and regional cuisine (€28–38 per person) — reservations essential

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is a completely different landscape from the coast — lush, green, and cool. The medronho distilleries along the road sell bottles for €8–15 — great souvenirs. The road to Fóia is winding — drive carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Faro (45 min) — the Algarve's capital. Visit the beautiful Cidade Velha (Old Town): the Arco da Vila, the Sé Catedral de Faro (climb the tower for rooftop views), and the haunting but fascinating Igreja dos Ossos (Chapel of Bones) inside the Igreja do Carmo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Faro's dock (Cais da Porta Nova) into the Ria Formosa Natural Park — a stunning lagoon system of barrier islands, saltpans, and bird-rich wetlands. Visit Ilha de Faro or Ilha Deserta (Ilha Barreta) for a swim on a pristine, unspoiled beach. Ferries run regularly (~€3–5 return).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Faro's charming marina area and waterfront for the evening. The city has a genuine local feel — less touristy than the western Algarve.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay before departing
meals.lunch: Tasca do Peixe in Faro — excellent fresh fish and seafood, very popular with locals, great value daily specials (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dois Irmãos in Faro — one of the oldest restaurants in the city (since 1925), classic Portuguese seafood and fish, historic atmosphere (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Faro is often overlooked by tourists who fly in and head straight to the beach resorts — it's a genuinely lovely city worth a full day. The Ria Formosa is a UNESCO-recognized ecosystem and home to the rare purple gallinule bird. Bring binoculars if you have them.

day_by_day.morning: Drive further east to Tavira (1 hour from Lagoa) — widely considered the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Stroll across the Roman bridge over the Gilão River, visit the Castelo de Tavira ruins and gardens, and explore the 37 churches that dot this elegant whitewashed town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Tavira's dock to Ilha de Tavira — a gorgeous barrier island beach in the Ria Formosa. The beach is long, wild, and relatively uncrowded in September. Swim, relax, and enjoy the peace. Ferries run frequently (~€2 return, 10-minute crossing).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Tavira for dinner — the town has an excellent restaurant scene with a more sophisticated, less touristy feel than the western Algarve.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay before departing, or stop at a café in Tavira
meals.lunch: Picnic on Ilha de Tavira — buy supplies at the Tavira market (Mercado da Ribeira) before taking the ferry: local olives, cheese, presunto ham, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Tavira — outstanding fresh fish and seafood on a riverside terrace, excellent regional wine list, very romantic setting (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is a 1-hour drive from Praia da Marinha — plan for a full day. The Mercado da Ribeira in Tavira is open in the mornings and is a wonderful place to browse local produce. September is an ideal time to visit Ilha de Tavira as summer crowds have thinned.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — return to Praia da Marinha for one last swim at this stunning cove. Take your time exploring the rock formations, sea arches, and pools you may have missed earlier in the trip. This is a morning to savor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Armação de Pêra (20 min east) and visit the Nossa Senhora da Rocha chapel — perched dramatically on a promontory above the sea. Then explore the Algar Seco natural rock formations near Carvoeiro — a labyrinth of eroded limestone platforms, blowholes, and sea pools accessible on foot from a clifftop car park.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Carvoeiro. Dress up slightly and choose your favorite restaurant from the week, or try somewhere new for a special final evening. Enjoy a bottle of Algarve wine and reflect on the trip.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay — enjoy a leisurely final full breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach snack bar at Praia da Marinha or Praia de Carvoeiro
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nortada in Carvoeiro — excellent seafood, beautiful clifftop terrace, perfect for a special farewell dinner (€28–40 per person) — reservations recommended

day_by_day.notes: Algar Seco is free to visit and most impressive at low tide — check tide times before going. Stock up on souvenirs in Carvoeiro village: local wines, medronho, flor de sal (Algarve sea salt), almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), and carob products are all excellent choices.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — pack up and check out of the boutique stay. Drive to Lagoa town for a last coffee and pastel de nata at a local café. If time allows, browse the Sunday market in Lagoa or pick up any last-minute souvenirs or wine bottles from the Lagoa Cooperative.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Faro Airport (45 min) allowing plenty of time for car return and check-in. Reflect on 13 wonderful days in the Algarve — stunning beaches, excellent wines, historic towns, and memorable meals.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay or a café in Lagoa — final galão and pastel de nata
meals.lunch: Light meal at Faro Airport or a café near the airport before departure
meals.dinner: On the plane or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for car return and check-in at Faro Airport. The airport is small but can get busy on Sunday afternoons with charter flights. Duty-free at Faro Airport has a decent selection of Portuguese wines and spirits at good prices — a last chance to stock up.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded coves for a refreshing swim.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (approx. 45 minutes). Settle into your suite, unpack, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the property.
day_by_day.afternoon: After freshening up, take a leisurely first stroll down to Praia da Marinha beach (a short walk from the boutique stay). Admire the iconic golden limestone cliffs and turquoise waters. Dip your toes in the Atlantic and soak in the dramatic scenery at your own relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset aperitivo on your private terrace or the hotel's terrace overlooking the coastline. Head to dinner at a nearby acclaimed restaurant in Carvoeiro or Lagoa for a refined introduction to Algarvian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: N/A — arrival day
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack or charcuterie board arranged by the boutique stay upon arrival
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro) — one Michelin-starred restaurant offering creative modern Portuguese tasting menus with exceptional local wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-booked. Request an early check-in if possible given the 13:00 arrival. Confirm dinner reservation at Bon Bon well in advance as it books up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — embark on the stunning Seven Hanging Valleys trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos), one of the Algarve's most celebrated coastal walks. Marvel at sea caves, natural arches, and hidden grottos carved into the golden cliffs. Swim at secluded coves accessible only on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the boutique stay for a luxurious poolside lunch. Spend the afternoon at leisure on Praia da Marinha beach, renting a kayak or stand-up paddleboard to explore the sea caves and rock formations from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel terrace. Dinner in the charming village of Carvoeiro, exploring its whitewashed streets before settling into a premium seafood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — fresh pastries, local cheeses, Alentejo charcuterie, freshly squeezed orange juice, and specialty Portuguese coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the boutique stay — grilled fresh catch of the day, salads, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo (Carvoeiro) — elevated seafood and traditional Algarvian dishes with panoramic ocean views and a curated Portuguese wine list

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring sunscreen, water, and a hat for the coastal hike. The hike is approximately 5.7 km and takes 2–3 hours. Sea conditions permitting for kayaking.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat tour departing from Benagil or Portimão — explore the legendary Algarve sea caves including the famous Benagil Cave (Algar de Benagil), accessible only by boat or kayak. Your private skipper will navigate through grottos, hidden beaches, and dramatic coastal arches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at a secluded beach accessible only by boat for a private picnic lunch prepared by the boutique stay. Swim in crystal-clear waters in total seclusion before returning by boat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a spa treatment — book a traditional Portuguese massage or a couples' treatment using local argan and carob oil products. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Lagoa town.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Gourmet private picnic basket prepared by the hotel — local cheeses, smoked swordfish, regional olives, artisan bread, and a chilled bottle of Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste (Ferragudo) — sophisticated riverfront dining with exceptional seafood and a remarkable Portuguese wine cellar overlooking the Arade River estuary

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a private boat charter through the hotel concierge. Bring a light layer for the boat ride as sea breezes can be cool. Confirm spa appointment in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — one of the Algarve's most beautiful historic towns. Explore the old town's Moorish walls, the Igreja de Santo António (a stunning baroque church), and the Slave Market Museum. Stroll along the Avenida dos Descobrimentos waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ponta da Piedade — Lagos's most spectacular coastal landmark. Walk the clifftop paths and descend the steps to the turquoise lagoons below. Optionally hire a small boat from local fishermen to explore the sea stacks and arches up close. Swim at Praia Dona Ana, one of the most photographed beaches in Portugal.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos's vibrant old town at a premium restaurant. Return to Praia da Marinha by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Cantinho do Mar (Lagos) — relaxed but refined beachfront dining with fresh grilled fish and regional specialties
meals.dinner: No Pátio (Lagos) — intimate, award-winning restaurant in a historic courtyard serving creative contemporary Portuguese cuisine with outstanding wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is approximately 30–35 minutes from Praia da Marinha by car. Arrange private driver for the day for maximum comfort and flexibility. Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting experience in the Lagoa wine region — the Algarve's most celebrated wine-producing area. Visit Adega do Cantor (Sir Cliff Richard's famous estate) or Quinta dos Vales for a private guided tour of the vineyards, cellars, and winemaking facilities, followed by a structured premium tasting of regional varieties including Negra Mole, Castelão, and Aragonez.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine journey with a visit to a second boutique winery — Quinta da Penina or Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — for a comparative tasting of Algarve DOC wines paired with local artisan products including regional cheeses, fig preserves, and smoked meats.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a private wine and cheese pairing curated by the hotel sommelier on your terrace as the sun sets over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Winery estate lunch at Quinta dos Vales — a farm-to-table spread of Algarvian specialties paired with estate wines in the vineyard setting
meals.dinner: In-room or terrace private dining experience arranged by the boutique stay — a curated multi-course menu celebrating local Algarvian produce with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book private winery tours well in advance. A private driver is essential for a full day of wine tasting. Quinta dos Vales also has an impressive sculpture garden worth exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Beach relaxation morning at Praia da Marinha — reserve a premium sun lounger setup with parasol, chilled towels, and a dedicated beach attendant through the hotel. Take a morning swim in the sheltered coves and enjoy the golden cliffs in the soft early light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Silves — the Algarve's ancient Moorish capital. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Wander through the charming town, visit the Gothic cathedral, and browse the local artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves at a premium restaurant celebrating the town's rich culinary heritage. Return to Praia da Marinha.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Beachside luxury picnic at Praia da Marinha — arranged by the hotel with chilled seafood, regional bread, and sparkling Algarve rosé
meals.dinner: Marisqueira Rui (Silves) — legendary and beloved seafood restaurant known for exceptional cataplana (traditional copper pot stew), grilled lobster, and an extensive Portuguese wine list

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 20 minutes inland from Praia da Marinha. The castle is particularly atmospheric in the late afternoon golden hour. September is ideal for visiting as summer crowds have thinned.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga or meditation session on the clifftops above Praia da Marinha — arrange through the hotel for a private instructor to guide a session as the sun rises over the Atlantic and illuminates the golden cliffs. Follow with a long, leisurely swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of continental Europe and one of Portugal's most dramatic landscapes. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres, walk the windswept clifftops, and stand at the lighthouse at Cabo de São Vicente where the Atlantic stretches endlessly westward.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a clifftop bar in Sagres watching the legendary Sagres sunset — famous for being one of the most spectacular in Europe. Dinner in Sagres before returning to Praia da Marinha.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Restaurante Memmo Baleeira (Sagres) — stylish hotel restaurant with stunning ocean views, fresh seafood, and a refined menu celebrating local ingredients
meals.dinner: A Sagres (Sagres village) — intimate restaurant known for exceptional grilled fish, percebes (barnacles), and regional wines in a rustic-chic setting

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 1 hour 15 minutes from Praia da Marinha. Arrange private driver for the day. Bring a light jacket as Cabo de São Vicente can be very windy even in September. The sunset here is truly unmissable.

day_by_day.morning: Private surf or stand-up paddleboard lesson at Praia de Carvoeiro or Praia do Carvalho — arranged through the hotel with a certified premium instructor. September offers ideal Atlantic swells for beginners and intermediate surfers alike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Algar Seco rock formations near Carvoeiro — a remarkable natural landscape of eroded limestone formations, sea pools, and caves directly on the clifftop. Walk the short trail and swim in the natural rock pools. Browse the boutiques in Carvoeiro village.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo at a clifftop bar in Carvoeiro. Premium dinner at one of the area's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marquise (Carvoeiro) — relaxed terrace dining with fresh seafood and traditional Portuguese dishes overlooking the village beach
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro) — return visit for the chef's seasonal tasting menu (if not visited on Day 1), or explore the degustation menu with wine pairing for a full Michelin experience

day_by_day.notes: Book surf/SUP lesson through the hotel concierge. Algar Seco is a 10-minute drive from Praia da Marinha and is best visited outside peak midday hours for the best light and fewer visitors.

day_by_day.morning: Private wine and food pairing masterclass — arrange through a local premium culinary school or wine educator for an intimate session at the boutique stay or a nearby quinta. Focus on Algarve and Alentejo wine regions, learning to identify varietals, terroir characteristics, and food pairing principles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Portimão and the Museu de Portimão — an award-winning museum built within a former sardine canning factory, offering fascinating insight into the Algarve's fishing and industrial heritage. Stroll along the Portimão waterfront and browse the marina.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Portimão at a premium waterfront restaurant. Evening stroll along the illuminated marina.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Tasca da Dona Barca (Portimão) — celebrated local institution famous for the finest grilled sardines in the Algarve, a quintessential Portuguese experience
meals.dinner: Restaurante Luar da Foia (near Monchique) — if venturing slightly further, this mountain restaurant offers exceptional views and game dishes; alternatively Vista (Portimão) for contemporary fine dining

day_by_day.notes: The wine masterclass can be arranged for 2–3 hours in the morning. Portimão is approximately 20 minutes from Praia da Marinha. The Museu de Portimão is genuinely world-class and not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Serra de Monchique — the lush mountain range rising dramatically above the Algarve coast. Drive through eucalyptus and cork oak forests to the spa town of Caldas de Monchique. Visit the historic thermal spa and enjoy a therapeutic thermal bath treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the summit of Fóia — the highest point in the Algarve at 902m — for panoramic views stretching from the Atlantic coast to the Spanish border on a clear September day. Explore the charming village of Monchique and visit local artisan workshops producing traditional wooden folding chairs (cadeiras de tesoura).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Praia da Marinha via the scenic coastal road. Sunset drinks at the hotel terrace. Relaxed premium dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central (Monchique) — beloved mountain restaurant serving hearty Algarvian mountain cuisine including roast kid (cabrito), presunto (cured ham), and medronho (arbutus berry spirit)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Leão de Porches (Porches) — intimate and sophisticated restaurant near the hotel celebrating local seasonal ingredients with a refined touch

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is approximately 45 minutes from Praia da Marinha. The mountain air is noticeably cooler — bring a light layer. The medronho brandy produced locally is a unique regional spirit worth sampling responsibly.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning of pure beach luxury at Praia da Marinha — your last full days at this extraordinary beach. Premium lounger setup, morning swim in the sheltered coves, snorkeling among the rock formations to spot octopus, sea bream, and other marine life. Rent snorkeling equipment through the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Porches Pottery (Olaria Algarve) near the hotel — one of Portugal's most celebrated traditional pottery workshops, famous for its hand-painted blue and white azulejo-inspired ceramics. Take a private workshop to paint your own piece as a unique luxury souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-to-the-beach sunset cocktail ceremony on the clifftops above Praia da Marinha. Premium dinner at a special restaurant to mark the penultimate evening.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Beachside seafood lunch at a nearby chiringuito — fresh grilled sea bass, prawns, and a bottle of chilled Algarve white wine with your feet in the sand
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste (Ferragudo) — return to this exceptional riverfront restaurant for a final celebratory dinner with a premium wine selection from their cellar

day_by_day.notes: Porches Pottery is just 5 minutes from Praia da Marinha and is a wonderful way to bring home a meaningful, handcrafted luxury souvenir. Book the pottery workshop in advance.
